meta.notes: Preliminary assessment based on web demo experiments and technical documentation. Evaluated 3 days after MusicGen to enable direct comparison of text-to-audio paradigms.

system_identification.primary_use_case: Text-to-audio music generation via spectrogram synthesis

technical_architecture.model_type: Fine-tuned Stable Diffusion v1.5 for spectrogram generation
technical_architecture.generation_mode: Batch processing (web demo) or local CLI
technical_architecture.training_data: Audio converted to spectrograms (dataset details limited in public documentation)

architecture_details.encoder: VAE encoder compresses audio spectrograms to latent space
architecture_details.decoder: VAE decoder reconstructs spectrograms from latent representations
architecture_details.denoiser: U-Net with cross-attention for text conditioning

interface_characteristics.interaction_paradigm: Text prompt → generate → download audio (batch processing)
interface_characteristics.learning_curve: Low - simple web interface with text box and parameter sliders

hardware_requirements.minimum_gpu: NVIDIA GPU with 6GB+ VRAM (for local deployment)
hardware_requirements.cpu_only_mode: Possible but very slow (generation >5 minutes per output)
hardware_requirements.storage_requirements: ~5GB for model weights (Stable Diffusion base + Riffusion fine-tune)
hardware_requirements.accessibility_barrier: Moderate - web demo accessible to all, local deployment requires GPU

input_output_characteristics.output_modality: Stereo audio (WAV format via spectrogram inversion)

composition.notes: Generates novel musical content from text, strong for short loops and rhythmic ideas

arrangement.notes: Can interpolate between prompts but limited structural control, 5.12s constraint limits arrangement utility

sound_design.notes: Effective for rhythmic textures and electronic sounds, spectrogram approach enables creative timbral exploration

performance.notes: Batch processing only, 30-40s generation time incompatible with real-time performance

mixing_mastering.notes: Outputs raw generated audio, no mixing/mastering capabilities

denoising_strength.impact: Controls creativity vs. adherence to seed audio. Higher = more variation, lower = closer to seed

num_inference_steps.impact: Quality vs. speed tradeoff. More steps = higher quality, slower generation

guidance_scale.impact: Classifier-free guidance strength. Higher = stronger prompt adherence, lower = more creative freedom

seed.impact: Reproducibility - same seed + prompt = same output

prompt_interpolation.impact: Smoothly transition between two musical ideas/styles

usability.rationale: Web interface very accessible (text box + sliders), but 5.12s fixed duration and generation queue times unpredictable. Local deployment requires GPU setup. Simple for basic use, limited for production workflows.

generation_speed.rationale: ~35 seconds for 5.12s output on web demo (real-time factor ~0.15x). Faster than MusicGen (140s for 30s), enabling more rapid iteration. Local deployment with RTX 3060 yields ~30s generation.
generation_speed.evidence: Web demo timing tests, comparison to MusicGen

audio_quality.rationale: Spectrogram inversion (Griffin-Lim) introduces phase artifacts and high-frequency smearing. Rhythmic elements clean, harmonic content has noticeable artifacts. 44.1kHz output better than MusicGen's 32kHz but spectrogram resolution limits detail.
audio_quality.evidence: Generated demo outputs, comparison to MusicGen

semantic_alignment.rationale: Initial tests show strong rhythmic interpretation ('funk drum groove' → syncopated drums), weak harmonic specificity ('minor 9th chords' → generic minor chords). Domain-specific strengths like MusicGen but different domains.
semantic_alignment.evidence: Preliminary prompt experiments with rhythm vs. harmony prompts

steerability.rationale: Denoising strength and guidance scale provide some control. Prompt interpolation enables creative blending. But text prompt remains primary control, with similar unpredictability to MusicGen. Parameters functional but coarse-grained.
steerability.evidence: Parameter exploration, web demo slider tests

workflow_impact.rationale: Faster generation (35s vs. MusicGen 140s) reduces waiting time. But 5.12s fixed duration requires multiple generations for longer clips. Web demo workflow simpler than MusicGen CLI but queue times variable. Moderate disruption expected.
workflow_impact.evidence: Workflow projection based on web demo experience

daw_integration.rationale: Web-based generation requires manual download → import to DAW. No tempo/key metadata like MusicGen. No plugin format. 5.12s fixed duration awkward for loop-based production (not 4 or 8 bars). Poor integration anticipated.

creative_adaptability.rationale: Spectrogram approach enables creative exploration (visual + audio). Prompt interpolation supports idea blending. But 5.12s constraint and domain biases (rhythm > harmony) may limit adaptability. Expecting moderate flexibility.
creative_adaptability.evidence: Demo experiments with varied prompts, interpolation feature testing

known_limitations: 5.12-second fixed duration - cannot specify custom lengths, awkward for loop-based production
Spectrogram resolution tradeoffs - time-frequency compromise limits detail
Griffin-Lim phase artifacts - high-frequency smearing, reduced harmonic clarity
Weak bass generation - spectrogram low-frequency limitations restrict bass range
Mid-phrase starts/ends - outputs often cut incomplete musical phrases
No tempo/key parameters - cannot specify BPM or harmonic center
Web demo queue unpredictability - generation times vary by server load (30s - 5 minutes)
GPU dependency for local use - web demo accessible but local deployment requires hardware
known_strengths: Fast generation - 30-40s for 5.12s output, ~4x faster than MusicGen
Accessible web interface - no installation/setup required for basic use
Strong rhythmic generation - drums, percussion, syncopated patterns excel
Prompt interpolation - unique feature for blending musical ideas smoothly
Open source - code and model available for modification/research
Spectrogram visualization - visual feedback for creative exploration
44.1kHz output - higher sample rate than MusicGen (32kHz)
evidence_sources: Forsgren, S., & Martiros, H. (2022). Riffusion - Stable diffusion for real-time music generation. arXiv preprint.
Riffusion Team. (2024). Riffusion Repository. GitHub. https://github.com/riffusion/riffusion

next_steps.phase_1_focus: Conduct 8 creative sessions generating funk elements (drums, rhythmic textures, synth patterns) to assess rhythmic strengths and harmonic weaknesses
hypotheses_to_test: Spectrogram artifacts more pronounced in harmonic content than rhythmic elements
5.12s duration constraint will require creative workarounds (concatenation, looping)
Prompt interpolation feature useful for exploring timbral variations
Faster generation enables more exploratory workflow than MusicGen
next_steps.documentation_strategy: 152-widget session log, focus on rhythmic vs. harmonic generation comparison, prompt interpolation experiments

reflexive_notes.evaluator_positionality: Web interface accessibility lowers barrier compared to MusicGen CLI, but my funk bass production needs may expose Riffusion's weak bass generation. Faster iteration may feel more creative than MusicGen's waiting periods.
reflexive_notes.methodological_concerns: 5.12s fixed duration is unique constraint not present in other systems - may require adaptation of evaluation methodology. Need to test concatenation strategies.
questions_raised: Will faster generation (35s vs. 140s) meaningfully improve creative workflow?
Can prompt interpolation compensate for semantic alignment gaps?
How much does spectrogram visualization aid creative process vs. distract?
